desk.none_for_you: No workflow actions for your role.
desk.group.desk_help: These steps move the edition between the writer, the desk editor, and copy. Readers do not see it.
desk.group.publish_help: These steps put this edition on the site, or set the time the worker will. A legal hold blocks schedule, publish, and republish.
desk.group.live_help: Archive and unarchive move this edition off the active desks, or back to unpublished. Taking it off the site is a separate card.
desk.group.stop_help: These steps end the edition. A story that has been published cannot be killed or deleted.
desk.card.hold: This does not take the story off the site. Readers still see a published edition. It blocks schedule, publish, and republish until an editor records that counsel signed off. An update to a story that is already live stays allowed. Choosing Legal cause when you take the story down is a different action: that one removes the edition.
desk.card.takedown: This removes the edition from the site. The address returns 410. A written reason and a reason code are required. Republish is a separate step, and a legal hold blocks it. A legal hold does not remove the story.
desk.card.takedown_legal: Legal cause means this edition is coming off the site for a legal reason. It is not a legal hold. A hold leaves a live story up and only blocks the next publish.
desk.help.submit: Sends this edition to the desk editor for news judgment. Readers still do not see it. You can withdraw it from review, but not after it reaches copy.
desk.help.withdraw: Pulls it back to a draft. Only from review. The writer can edit again. Readers do not see it.
desk.help.request_changes: Sends it back to the writer. A reason is required and is kept in the audit. Readers do not see it.
desk.help.send_to_copy: The ordinary path. Copy gets the text. Signing off later does not publish. Readers do not see it.
desk.help.return_to_writer: Copy sends it back. A reason is required. The writer edits and submits again. Readers do not see it.
desk.help.finish_copy: Copy has signed off. The edition is approved and still not on the site. An editor can publish or schedule it.
desk.help.approve: Skips copy. Used for breaking news. A reason is required and is the audit. Nothing is on the site yet.
desk.help.schedule: Sets a future publish time in UTC. An optional take-down time must be later. The worker publishes it. Cancel returns it to approved and clears both times. Refused while a legal hold is on.
desk.help.cancel_schedule: Returns the edition to approved and clears the publish time and the take-down time. Readers do not see it.
desk.help.publish: Puts this revision on the site. Readers see it. Refused while a legal hold is on. A later save stays on the working copy until you publish the update.
desk.help.publish_update: Points the live page at the working copy. Readers then see this revision. A public note is a separate step.
desk.help.unpublish: Takes the edition down. A written reason and a reason code are required. The address returns 410. Republish is a separate step.
desk.help.republish: Puts a taken-down edition back on the site. Refused while a legal hold is on.
desk.help.kill: Spikes the edition before it has ever been live. A reason is required. It stays in the record. Impossible if this edition was ever published.
desk.help.archive: Takes a published, unpublished, or killed edition off the active desks. The public address then returns not found, which is different from a 410 takedown.
desk.help.unarchive: Returns an archived edition to unpublished, not to the status it had before. Readers still do not see it until someone republishes.
desk.help.delete: Removes the writer’s own draft that was never published. Prefer kill when an editor spikes it. A story that has been published cannot be deleted.
desk.restored: Restored as a new revision. The live page is unchanged until you publish the update.
desk.slug_changed: Slug updated. The old address redirects here.
desk.corrected: Note added. Readers see it on the live page.

flow.title: How a story gets published
flow.intro: Each language of a story has its own status. Arabic can be live while English is still a draft. Readers only see a published edition.
flow.ordinary_help: Most stories take this path. The desk can leave it. This is the default.
flow.step.draft: The writer files the headline and the text. Each manual save appends a revision. The writer can edit a draft, and a story that was sent back.
flow.step.review: The desk editor judges the story. The writer can withdraw it to a draft. They cannot edit the text while it sits here.
flow.step.copy: Copy fixes language, the headline, and style. Signing off does not publish.
flow.step.approved: Copy has signed off, or the desk skipped copy with a written reason. Nothing is on the site yet. Publish now is available from here.
flow.step.scheduled: An editor sets a future time, in UTC. The worker publishes it. Two workers cannot publish the same row.
flow.step.published: Readers see this revision only. A later save stays on the working copy until an editor publishes the update.
flow.back.title: Sent back
flow.back.body: The desk editor requests changes from review, from copy, or from approved. Copy sends it back with “Return to writer”, and a reason is required. The writer edits and submits again. Withdraw is only from review, back to draft.
flow.skip.title: Breaking news
flow.skip.body: Approve from review skips copy and requires a reason. That reason is the audit. Copy can still clean a later revision, and an editor publishes the update.
flow.embargo.title: Embargo
flow.embargo.body: Schedule needs a future publish time. A take-down time is optional and must be later. Cancel returns the story to approved and clears both times. A legal hold blocks schedule, publish, and republish. The worker also skips a scheduled row while the hold is on.
flow.spike.title: Kill and delete
flow.spike.body: Kill is an editorial spike, with a reason, from any state before the story has ever been live. Delete removes the writer’s own never-published draft. A story that has been published cannot be killed or deleted. Taking it down is a separate action.
flow.after_help: Publishing is not the end of the record.
flow.update: A new save does not change the public page. Publish update points the live revision at the working copy. A public note — correction, clarification, or update — is separate from the text.
flow.takedown: Take down needs a written reason and a code: legal, major error, duplicate, safety, or other. The address returns 410. Republish is a separate audited action, and a legal hold blocks it. An expired embargo is taken down by the worker, with the reason “Embargo expired”.
flow.archive: Archive takes a published, unpublished, or killed edition off the active desks. The public address then returns “not found”, which is different from a 410 takedown. Unarchive returns it to unpublished, not to the status it had before.
flow.slug: Changing the address after publication keeps the old address as a redirect.
flow.hold_body: A flag, not a status. The story can still move through review and copy. Schedule, publish, and republish wait until an editor records that counsel signed off. An update to a story that is already live stays allowed.
flow.languages_body: The English edition is another row on the same story. It has its own address, schedule, revisions, and history.
flow.role.writer: Files the story, edits their own draft, submits, withdraws, and deletes their own never-published draft. On a live story they can save a proposal. They cannot publish it.
flow.role.copy: Works the copy desk, returns the text, and signs off. Cannot publish.
flow.role.editor: Accepts the story, sends it to copy, requests changes, skips copy, and kills it. Publishing needs the publish permission. A grant can be limited to one section.
flow.role.archive: Archive and unarchive are a separate permission from publish.
flow.table_help: This list is the state machine the desk enforces. An action that is not here is refused.
flow.owner: Marked actions can be done by the writer on their own story. Someone who can edit any story in scope can do them too.
